Learning-guided nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II for
multi-objective satellite range scheduling problem
Yan-Jie Song a, Xin Ma a, Xun-Jia Li a, Li-Ning Xing a,*, Pei Wang b
a College of Systems Engineering, National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, 410073, Hunan, China
b Unit 75831, Guangzhou, 510510, Guangdong, China
A R T I C L E I N F O
Keywords:
Learning-guided
Multi-objective
NSGA-II
Satellite range scheduling
Evolutionary
Algorithm
A B S T R A C T
Satellite range scheduling is an important issue in the ﬁeld of satellite mission planning, which greatly affects the
development of satellite industry. This paper analyzed satellite range scheduling problem, constructed a multi-
objective SRSP (MO-SRSP) model and proposed an improved multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA),
called learning-guided nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II (LGNSGAII) that contains a learning mecha-
nism. Learning mechanisms can speed up optimization process. Meanwhile, another algorithm called task-time
window selection algorithm (TTSA) is also proposed. Speciﬁcally, it can select satellite ground stations time
windows for tasks. TTSA includes three location selection methods and two location movement methods, both are
used to select the appropriate execution location for tasks. Experiments show that the proposed algorithm can
solve MO-SRSP better than several comparison algorithms. In other words, this algorithm we proposed has a
broad practical application prospect.
1. Introduction
Satellites meet military and civilian mission requirements by
providing a variety of services, such as environmental monitoring,
disaster prediction, satellite navigation. Daily service of satellites relies
on the communication between satellite ground stations and satellites.
This communication process with satellite ground station is called sat-
ellite range, or satellite measurement and control. In this paper, an
optimization problem, which is also known as Satellite TT&C scheduling
problem, is named satellite range scheduling problem. In SRSP, the goal
that match many satellite resources with measurement and control re-
sources, and select appropriate measurement and control tasks to com-
plete, is the key to ensure normal operation and successful completion of
various missions. Using satellite resources efﬁciently is of great signiﬁ-
cance for the development of satellite industry and for humanity.
SRSP is to select appropriate location and time for satellites’
communication with ground stations. More generally, it needs to deter-
mine the time for satellites communicating with ground stations.
Communication between satellite and station must be carried out at a
position where two antennas are visible to each other. This time interval
is called ground station visible time window. Satellite measurement and
control tasks must be done within the range of visible time windows of
ground stations. Numerous measurement and control requirements
combined with the limited resources of ground stations make SRSP hard
to solve, thus followed by oversubscribed scheduling problem. Mean-
while, SRSP has limitations on technology and equipment. These con-
straints increase the complexity of this problem. Although this problem
can be solved by an exact solution algorithm in the case of small-scale
tasks, it is difﬁcult to obtain a feasible solution in a limited time once
the task scale is increased. In contrast, evolutionary algorithms are more
suitable to solve SRSP.
Satellite range scheduling problem has always been an important
focus in the ﬁeld of satellite mission planning. This problem is similar to
vehicle routing problem with time windows (VRPTW) [31]. However,
MO-SRSP will cause tasks to fail due to high resources of the mission
relative to ground stations. And there is no problem of vehicle movement
in this problem, but the choice of time window resources. Due to
different backgrounds of problem, our problem and model are more
complicated than VRPTW problem. Dynamic optimization process of
some complex systems is also useful for reference [24,25]. This problem
has two major characteristics, one is oversubscribed scheduling, the
other is that the problem belongs to a NP-Hard problem, and these two
points have been conﬁrmed by the research [1,2]. Oversubscribed
scheduling means that the number of tasks that need to be planned

exceeds the maximum number that the system can complete, and there
will be a failure of some tasks. This problem not only has theoretical
research signiﬁcance but also is a complex practical engineering prob-
lem. Satellite measurement and control scheduling research conducted
by AFSCN is an early and relatively complete study, which considers
low-orbit satellite range scheduling and high-orbit satellite range
scheduling [3,4]. In the research of SRSP scheduling algorithm, most of
the research focuses on single-objective optimization algorithm, while
only a small part of the research focuses on multi-objective optimization
algorithm. Related research involving single-objective optimization al-
gorithms is reﬂected in both exact solution algorithm and heuristic al-
gorithm [3,5–7]. Exact solution algorithm can get good results in
small-scale test scenarios, but it is very difﬁcult to get results in
large-scale scenarios [8]. As for heuristic algorithm, both heuristic-based
optimization algorithm and meta-heuristic algorithm can cope with
large-scale scenarios well [9–11]. [12] proposed a tabu search method to
solve the problem of satellite measurement and control mission planning.
Simulated annealing algorithms and genetic algorithm have also been
used to solve this problem [13]. In particular, genetic algorithm has been
proven to have a good solution [14,15]. [26] attempted to transform the
satellite measurement and control scheduling problem into a graph col-
oring problem, and a reasonable scheduling scheme was obtained by
using the graph coloring method. Satellite data downlink mission plan-
ning problems have strong similarities with satellite range scheduling
problem [27] considered the impact of task execution time on optimi-
zation objectives, the sooner a task is completed, the higher beneﬁt will
be. Authors proposed a variety of optimization strategies that not only
solve problems raised in the article, but also have strong applicability to
potential new constraints [28] modeled satellite range scheduling
problem from the perspective of satellite ground stations, and designing a
simulated annealing algorithm to solve this problem [29] proposed a new
ant colony algorithm to solve the problem by simulating the ant motion.
From the existing research on satellite range scheduling problem, it can
be seen that this problem is similar to other satellites area problems, such
as imaging satellite mission planning problem [30]. Models given by
different researchers are quite different, and data used in experiments is
also set by themselves. Only public data set today is AFSCN (2005),
which can be obtained through the website: http://www.cs.colostate.
edu/sched/data.html. This data set is rarely used in research today
because the scale of tasks is small, and the simpliﬁcation of data set for
actual scenes has little guiding signiﬁcance for the application.
Methods used by the researchers can be divided into exact solution
algorithms and approximate solution algorithms. As measurement and
control tasks increase rapidly under conditions of increasing measure-
ment and control resources, research on exact solution algorithms in
recent years is rare. An important reason is that the algorithm fails to
achieve good results in a short time in a large-scale task scenario.
Approximate solution algorithm can be mainly divided into three cate-
gories, a heuristic algorithm using rules, evolutionary optimization al-
gorithm and the above two hybrid algorithms. Hybrid algorithms take
into account advantages of the ﬁrst two algorithms and overcomes
shortcomings of using an algorithm alone, which can achieve good
planning results in large-scale task scenarios.
Multi-objective optimization algorithm to solve multi-objective SRSP
(MO-SRSP) research is few and this area need further study [16] pro-
posed a multi-objective heuristic neighborhood search algorithm to solve
satellite observation mission planning problems [17] took the Chinese
navigation satellite system as the research object, and proposed an
evolutionary multi-objective algorithm [18] proposed a novel imaging
scheduling algorithm of multi-objective optimization for multi-satellite
(MOO-MS) to solve multiple imaging satellite scheduling problems
[19] analyzed the electronic reconnaissance satellites scheduling prob-
lem (ERSSP), established a model and proposed a Monte Carlo simulation
based multi-objective extremal optimization (MCSBMOEO) algorithm.
Existing research that uses multi-objective optimization algorithm to
solve SRSP is still little, and single-objective optimization algorithm can
only solve the problem from the perspective of task proﬁt or task
completion, which is not comprehensive enough compared to multi-
objective algorithm. This research focus on constructing a multi-
objective mathematical model and proposing a multi-objective solving
algorithm.
Contributions of this paper include: (1) A mathematical model of
multi-objective SRSP, proposing hypothesis conditions, objective func-
tion and constraints is constructed; (2) A learning-guided NSGA-II algo-
rithm (LGNSGAII) based on multi-objective optimization algorithm is
proposed; (3) A heuristic algorithm for task selection time window is
given; (4) Feasibility and efﬁciency of the proposed algorithm are proved
by simulation experiments.
The structure of this paper is as follows. In the second part, SRSP will
be introduced and a multi-objective SRSP (MO-SRSP) will be proposed.
For MO-SRSP, a speciﬁc solution algorithm will be given in the third part.
Planning effect of the algorithm will be tested in the fourth part. In the
ﬁnal section, some ﬁndings and prospects will be discussed.
2. Problem deﬁnition and mathematical model
2.1. Description of SRSP
Satellite ground station completes the process of monitoring satel-
lites’ status through measurement and control and uploads mission in-
structions for satellites. Satellite range scheduling allows satellites to
operate well in orbit and complete mission requests. Firstly, we take two
satellites and one satellite ground station as an example. One of the two
satellites is a low-orbit satellite and the other is a high-orbit satellite.
Each of the two satellites needs to complete a measurement and control
task. As shown in Fig. 1, the low-orbit satellite has a shorter time window
due to the lower altitude of ﬂight orbit, while the available time window
for the high-orbit satellite measurement and control tasks is longer. When
LEO1 and GEO1 in the ﬁgure pass through the same satellite ground
station one by one, it is necessary to select an appropriate execution time
for measurement and control tasks of these two satellites, so that both
measurement and control tasks can be performed as successful as
possible.
During a certain measurement and control cycle, there are many
available time windows for ground stations that can be used for mea-
surement and control opportunities. Each measurement and control task
request must be made within the visible time window of the ground
station. When a task occupies part or all of a ground station time window
position, other tasks will no longer be able to select this time window
position. At the same time, since measurement and control tasks need to
be carried out within a certain time range, the position of the ground
station time window available for each measurement and control task is
limited. In addition, the ground station antenna needs to match with the
satellite antenna to execute the measurement and control tasks. That is to
say, the ground station needs to rotate the antenna to a certain angle after
performing a task before the next measurement and control task can be
performed.
2.2. Mathematical model for multi-objective SRSP (MO-SRSP)
Given two sets Task and Timewindow, respectively represent the set of
measurement and control tasks and the set of ground station time win-
dows. There are L satellites in the measurement and control tasks set, and
the i-th satellite has Mi tasks, and there are a total of O tasks. For each
measurement task taski;j, i and j represent the i-th satellite and the j-th
task, respectively. Each of tasks has a time range attribute ½esti;j; leti;j,
where esti;j indicates the earliest time at which the task can be started,
and leti;j indicates that the task should be completed no later than the

latest time. Each measurement and control task also has an attribute of
task time length leni;j, and each measurement and control task needs to
meet the length of time before it can be considered as successful execu-
tion. In addition, task also has a value attribute, which is called “proﬁt”,
represented by pi;j. Task proﬁt is related to many factors such as the
importance of task and the length of task. There are a total of Q available
time windows in the ground station time window set. For the k-th
available time window, there is also a time range attribute ½Etk; Ltk.
Among them, Etk indicates the earliest visible time of a satellite ground
station, and Ltk indicates the latest visible time of a satellite ground
station. Each measurement and control task should be carried out within
the visible time range of satellite ground stations. Tasks are independent
of each other. When one task occupies time window resources, another
task cannot use this available time window and needs to wait for a certain
time. This process is called task switching. In the process of switching
among different measurement and control tasks, satellite ground station
antennas need to be rotated, which is deﬁned as the task conversion time
δ. Start time of the latter task cannot be earlier than the time when an-
tenna rotation can perform the next task.
Multi-objective SRSP has two decision variables. One is xi;j, indicating
whether the j-th task of the i-th satellite is executed. If the measurement
and control task can be performed, xi;j is 1, otherwise, xi;j is 0. Another
decision variable is si;j, which indicates the start execution time of the j-th
task of the i-th satellite. After deciding the execution of each measure-
ment and control task and the time of the task, an execution plan of task
sequence can be obtained, and speciﬁc execution planning of each task in
the measurement and control task set is included in the solution.
In order to transform SRSP problem from a complex engineering
problem into a scientiﬁc problem that facilitates the construction of
mathematical models. The following assumptions are required:
1. Only consider satellite measurement and control problems, other
imaging observation and data downlink processes will not affect the
measurement and control;
2. All devices are in normal operation, and the failure of the measure-
ment and control tasks caused by factors such as equipment operation
failures is not considered;
3. Once a measurement and control task begins, it will not be allowed to
end halfway;
4. After a task starts, it cannot be preempted by other tasks;
5. Ignoring the time required for satellite and satellite ground stations to
construct communication links, only considering the planning and
scheduling process;
6. Satellite power can support the needs of measurement and control
tasks;
7. Rotation of the antenna requires a certain conversion time, which
cannot be ignored.
Multi-objective SRSP (MO-SRSP) reference the literature [14,15,21]
optimization objectives, mainly include two optimization objectives: (1)
overall proﬁt of the task sequence; (2) task failure rate in the task
sequence. For the ﬁrst optimization goal, the maximum proﬁt of the task
sequence should be achieved. For the second optimization goal, if it has
the fewer failed tasks in the task sequence, the smaller the task failure
rates it will be. So far, we can build its mathematical model based on the
above description of MO-SRSP.

3. Method
To solve multi-objective SRSP (MO-SRSP), we gave two algorithms,
one is learning-guided NSGA-II (LGNSGAII) and the other is task-time
window selection algorithm (TTSA). LGNSGAII is used to continuously
generate new solutions and improve the performance of task scheduling.
TTSA is used to determine whether a task is executed, and the execution
time of the task. LGNSGAII will be introduced in Section 3.1. After that,
an introduction to TTSA will be given in Section 3.2.
3.1. Learning-guided NSGA-II (LGNSGAII)
3.1.1. Overall ﬂow of the algorithm
Learning-guided NSGA-II (LGNSGAII) is based on the classical NSGA-
II algorithm in multi-objective optimization algorithm and is adapted to
multi-objective SRSP (MO-SRSP) [33,35]. Learning mechanism is intro-
duced so that the algorithm can be optimized selectively. LGNSGAII is
ﬁrst initialized to get the initial population. Evolutionary search can
optimize population and produce offspring population, which is called
genetic operation, including selection, crossover, mutation, and so on.
The number of individuals within the population determined whether
the elite individuals in the population are selected by non-dominated
sorting and crowding distance sorting, and individual size of popula-
tion is ﬁxed at a stable number. An evolutionary search is then performed
to obtain a new generation of populations that are merged with the
previous generation's population for a new cyclical process. Flow chart of
LGNSGAII is shown in Fig. 2.
Before genetic operation, learning mechanism obtains the conﬂict
rate of task sequence, and automatically adjusts the weight of conﬂict
rate by using individual's performance. Both learning mechanism and
selection mechanism correspond to an individual. It can improve the task
selection of genetic operation a lot. In this way, the optimization process
can be made to have a deﬁnite purpose, so that the task sequence pro-
ceeds in the direction in which the task conﬂict is reduced. The learning
mechanism has a complexity of OðnÞ.
In order to adjust to the learning mechanism and problem, we gave
two crossover operators and two mutation operators. These operators are
matched to MO-SRSP. Crossover and mutation make task sequence not
fall into local optimum. Key steps in the speciﬁc LGNSGAII, genetic
operation and learning mechanisms will be described in the following
sections. The pseudo code of LGNSGAII is shown in Table of the algo-
rithm.

The coding mode of individuals in the population adopts real coding,
which means each position represents a measurement and control task.

3.1.3. Initial population generation
The initial solution is generated by a randomly generated method,
and the length of each solution is equal to the length of the task sequence.
Each measurement task is allocated to a location where task scheduling is
performed in a random manner. In this way, an initial planning scheme is
obtained, and the subsequent optimization process is performed after the
sequence is initialized.
3.1.4. Non-dominated sorting
Non-dominated sorting method reference the [20] proposed a fast
non-dominated sorting method. It is a sorting algorithm with complexity
Oðmn2Þ, where m represents the number of objectives and n represents
the number of individuals in the population. The non-dominated sorting
ﬁrst determines the dominating number to be the ﬁrst layer according to
the dominance number of each solution in the entire solution space. Then
it selects an individual from the ﬁrst layer and traverses its corresponding
dominating set for each individual the dominance number is subtracted
by 1. If dominance number becomes 0, the second layer is obtained. By
this way, we can get all layers. When comparing different results, we
prefer to a solution with a lower rank.

Calculation and sorting of crowding distance are carried out in each
dominating set. Crowding-distance means the density of an individual in
a dominant set, denoted by Γ½g. First, crowding distance of each indi-
vidual is initialized to zero. Thereafter, the individuals are sorted ac-
cording to the m-th objective function. Crowding distance of the ﬁrst and
last individual sorting result is deﬁned as positive inﬁnity. Then, the
formula for crowding distance from the second to the penultimate indi-
vidual is as shown in Formula (11).

3.1.8. Crossover
The crossover operation is performed inside the individual, and there
are two ways: between different segments (C1) and within the same
segments (C2). The task sequence selected for both crossover operations
is λ. For the crossover between segments, as shown in Fig. 4.
The ﬁrst way is the crossover in different segment, as is shown in
Fig. 4. Gray squares indicate that a task sequence in the ﬁrst segment and
a task sequence in the third segment are respectively selected by means of
random numbers. These two tasks are equal in length and a new sequence

The second way is the crossover within the same segment, as is shown
in Fig. 5. The positions of two crossover operations in the ﬁgure are all
within the same segment. A new generation of individuals can be ob-
tained by swapping the two segments.
If two segments overlap occurs in the process of crossover within the
same segment, one of the segments will be regenerated in a random
manner. We deﬁne a shift operation Θ that randomly moves the φ
backward (forward) if the selected segment contains the task or the last
task of the ﬁrst part of the task sequence and or length does not meet the
genetic operation requirements. Random movement generates a moving
distance randomly, when a moving operation is performed. The shift
operation is shown in Fig. 6.
New individuals can be generated by inter-segment and intra-
segment crossover operations, so that the population can evolve to-
ward better objective function values. Meanwhile, the crossover method
can prevent the population from falling into local optimum and cannot
jump out.

3.2. Task-time window selection algorithm (TTSA)
After each generation of a new population is obtained, the task
sequence needs to be matched to the available time window of ground
stations. Therefore, TTSA algorithm is embedded in LGNSGAII for use. In
other words, the execution time of each task is decided. If the available
time window cannot be selected to execute it, we should abandon this
task and start the planning process for the next task. The pseudo code of
TTSA is shown in Table of the algorithm.

task is attempted to move forward to ﬁnd the available position, and then
determine the task execution time, as shown in Fig. 12. S2 means that if
the task cannot perform the task at the current time window position, the
task is attempted to move backward to ﬁnd the available location, and
then the time to execute the task is determined, as shown in Fig. 13. If
there is still no time window available after movements, this task is not
executed and time window is selected for the next task.
4. Experiments and results
4.1. Experimental environment and experimental scenarios
Experimental environment: The proposed algorithms are imple-
mented by Matlab2017a on a desktop with Core I7-7700 3.6 GHz CPU,
8 GB memory, and Windows 7 operating system. Experimental examples
generated by STK are generated based on actual satellite application
scenarios.
Examples in this experimental part of this paper are close to the real
application scenarios. Taking measurement and control tasks within a
scheduling period as the planning goal, one of our cycles here is set to one
day, which is 24 h. In one day's time, we constructed test cases for mul-
tiple satellites and multiple ground stations. All measurement and control
tasks are generated according to the actual satellite operation. Initial
orbital parameters for a satellite are shown in Table 1. Locations of sat-
ellites in space are characterized by six orbital parameters: the length of
the semi-major axis (LSA), Eccentricity (E), inclination (I), argument of
perigee (AP), right ascension of the ascending node (RAAN), and mean
anomaly (MA). Satellites conclude two types: low-orbit satellites and
high-orbit satellites. Satellites and ground stations in the experiment are
all from China, and ground stations are only set up in China. Therefore,
the available time window resources of satellites are valuable. Satellites
can only perform measurement and control tasks when they pass through
China. Correspondingly, measurement and control tasks include low-
orbit satellite measurement and control tasks and high-orbit satellite
measurement and control tasks. In the meantime, we also consider
simultaneous existence of low-orbit satellites and high-orbit satellites,
which means that there are both two types of measurement and control
tasks, which is named as an integrated measurement and control task.
In this paper, different task scales are set for different types of mea-
surement and control tasks to test the performance of proposed
LGNSGAII. Task size includes scenarios of 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300,
500, and 1000 tasks.
4.2. Comparison algorithm
Comparison algorithms in this paper chooses four multi-objective
optimization algorithms. We selected NSGAII algorithm, MOEA/D algo-
rithm, MOEA/DD algorithm and MOMA/D algorithm respectively. Ge-
netic algorithms have a great performance in SRSP. NSGAII algorithm
and MOEA/D algorithm are optimum optimization methods in multi-
objective optimization algorithm [24,25]. MOEA/DD algorithm and
MOMA/D algorithm are multi-objective evolutionary algorithms with
very good optimization results in two recent studies, which are
state-of-the-art algorithms. The following is a brief introduction to
MOEA/D algorithm, MOEA/DD algorithm and MOMA/D algorithm.
MOEA/D algorithm: Multi-objective evolutionary algorithm based on
decomposition (MOEA/D) is an optimization algorithm for solving multi-
objectives proposed by Zhang in 2007 [22]. The core idea of this algo-
rithm is to transform a multi-objective optimization problem into a
single-objective optimization problem and perform simultaneous opti-
mization. This is a method that is sufﬁciently classic and optimized in
multi-objective optimization.
MOMA/D algorithm: It is a new algorithm proposed by Zhang [32],
named as multi-objective memetic algorithm based on decomposition for
big optimization problems (MOMA/D), is proposed. It is a new improved
memetic algorithm.
MOEA/DD algorithm: Deb [34] suggests a uniﬁed paradigm, which

from both of dominance- and decomposition-based approaches to bal-

4.4. Simulation results
This section will verify the algorithm effect of our proposed
LGNSGAII. Simulation experiment will use the algorithm to prepare and
schedule low-orbit satellite measurement and control tasks, high-orbit
satellite measurement and control tasks and integrated measurement
and control tasks under different task sizes. First, we conducted experi-
ments on low-orbit satellite measurement and control task scheduling.
Results are shown in Table 3.
In the experiment, each algorithm was run 30 times. The results table
shows the average value of the different algorithms for different functions,
the best value, the standard deviation (SD). We also compared the number
of non-dominated solutions obtained by the multi-objective optimization
algorithm. It can be seen from Table 3 that in the low-orbit satellite range
scheduling, the overall performance of multiple optimization algorithms is
relatively close. From the scale of 50–300 tasks, optimization effect of
LGNSGAII is the most ideal among several algorithms. When the task size is
50, all ﬁve algorithms can successfully complete the scheduling of all tasks
and select the appropriate execution time for tasks. As the size of tasks
increases, the number of failed tasks increases, but can be kept at a rela-
tively low level. It can be said that LGNSGAII can well complete low-orbit
satellite MO-SRSP. If we use a single objective algorithm, such as genetic
algorithm, it isdifﬁcult to balance different objectives. This reﬂects that the
single-objective optimization algorithm has certain limitations compared
to the multi-objective optimization algorithm. From the results, wecan also
see that all algorithms have less ﬂuctuation in the low-orbit satellite range
scheduling, and the standard deviation in each experimental scene is
relatively small. Because the single mission of low-orbit satellite mea-
surementandcontroltasks haslow proﬁts, localadjustmentofthe planning
scheme has little impact on the ﬁnal program progit. In the case of indi-
vidual experimental scenarios, there is a comparison algorithm superior to
LGNSGAII. For example, in the scenario where thetask size is 150 tasks, the
optimal planning result of MOMA/D in objective function 1 is better than
the proposed algorithm. In this case, the comparison algorithm can only
achieve one objective function value better than LGNSGGAII, and two
objective functions' values can't achieve the best results. Therefore, our
proposed algorithm can solve MO-SRSP problem better.
After that, we performed algorithm tests on the high-orbit satellite
range scheduling problem of different task scales. Results are shown in
Table 4. Compared with low-orbit satellite measurement and control
tasks, high-orbit satellite measurement and control tasks have longer
mission time lengths and mission proﬁts, and planning and scheduling
will be more difﬁcult. As can be seen from Table 4, high-orbit satellite
measurement and control task sequence with the same number of tasks
has a higher proﬁt, and is accompanied by a higher task failure rate. For
example, when the task size is 300, task failure rate after optimization
using LGNSGAII is still 34.7%. It can be seen from results that the pro-
posed algorithm has better applicability for more complex scenarios. In
the high-orbit satellite range scheduling experiment, optimization results
of the algorithm ﬂuctuate greatly, and task proﬁt and task failure rates of
different planning schemes change signiﬁcantly. It can be seen that the

other ﬁve algorithms.
After the low-orbit satellite range scheduling experiment, we
designed a range scheduling experiment under large-scale mission sce-
nario of high-orbit satellites, with a task size of 500 tasks and 1000 tasks.
Results are shown in Figs. 14–17. It can be seen from Fig. 14 and Fig. 15

Among the other four algorithms, NSGAII performs better in objective 1.

After that, we verify algorithm optimization speed. We compare CPU

5. Conclusion
Based on satellite measurement and control process, this paper pro-
poses a multi-objective SRSP (MO-SRSP) mathematical model. The ob-
jectives is to maximize task sequence proﬁt and minimize task failure
rate. We also give some constraints. After analyzing characteristics, we
propose a learning mechanism with a new index called task conﬂict rate
based on NSGAII algorithm. This learning mechanism can guide the
optimization process of evolutionary algorithms.
We have designed various types of experiments to verify effectiveness
of the proposed algorithm. It can be concluded from experimental result
that our algorithm is more ideal for low-orbit satellite and high-orbit
satellite range scheduling, which results a better optimization effect
and calculation speed. LGNSGAII has outstanding performance for
complex application scenarios, especially in large-scale application sce-
narios. We also carried out measurement and control scheduling for in-
tegrated tasks. Compared with classic MOMA/D algorithm, LGNSGAII is
more suitable for solving MO-SRSP.
In the following research, we will consider MO-SPSR problem with
more objective functions and give a high-efﬁciency solving algorithm for
high-dimensional optimization problems. Besides, how to get a more
evenly distributed Pareto front can be chosen as a research emphasis in
the future.
